title: Chocolate lava cakes
summary: Individual chocolate cakes baked hot and fast so the outside sets while the centre stays molten.

ingredients.note: plus a little for the ramekins

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Butter four 170 ml (6 oz) ramekins and dust them with the cocoa, tapping out the excess. Set them on a baking sheet.
Melt the butter and chocolate together over barely simmering water and stir until smooth. Whisk in the powdered erythritol.
In another bowl whisk the eggs, yolks, vanilla and salt for 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Whisk the warm chocolate into the eggs, then fold in the almond flour.
Divide among the ramekins. (They can be covered and chilled for up to a day at this point; add 2 minutes to the baking time.)
Bake 10–12 minutes, until the edges are firm and the centres still soft and slightly domed.
Rest 1–2 minutes, run a knife round each, and turn out onto plates. Serve straight away.
dairy_free_notes: Coconut oil makes a slightly firmer shell and a looser centre; check the cakes a minute early.
tips: Ovens vary a lot at this heat: bake one test cake first if you are serving guests.

origin.history: The molten-centred chocolate cake is a restaurant creation of the 1980s, and its origin is disputed. The French chef Michel Bras developed a chocolate 'coulant' with a frozen ganache centre in the early 1980s, while the New York chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten is often credited with popularising the underbaked version in 1987. By the 1990s it was on restaurant menus across the United States.
